sentence: This project studies which human endogenous retroviruses are active in clear cell Renal Cell Carcinoma tumors and whether they could act as tumor-specific antigens.
This project builds a microphysiologic system that grows salivary gland tissue with nerves in an array for toxicity testing and drug discovery.
This project tries to find out how DNA changes in blood cells relate to mild cognitive impairment, dementia and kidney disease.
This project tries to show that aging slows wound healing by weakening blood stem cells called hematopoietic stem cells in mice.
This project uses machine learning to study how natural product structure relates to activity and to repurpose natural products as protein-protein interaction inhibitors.
This project studies immune cell responses in dogs and humans with invasive urinary bladder cancer to improve immunotherapy.
This project builds a tool that uses statistical modeling and machine learning to predict whether patients will awaken from coma after cardiac arrest.
This project builds methods to read all kinds of RNA, including noncoding RNAs, in single cells to study how they drive hematopoiesis.
This project builds statistical and computational tools to find genetic effects in Alzheimer's disease that standard analyses often miss.
This project provides mass spectrometry services that measure proteins and metabolites to help study how diabetes develops.
This project uses natural variation in stress signaling in yeast to find out why some individuals are more susceptible to stress than others.
This project designs and builds bifunctional molecules that bring extracellular proteins close to cell-surface receptors.
This project studies how incomplete and inconsistent the reporting of harms in clinical trials is.
This project studies how axonal guidance signaling pathways control the movement and clustering of dermal condensates in developing hair follicles.
This project builds a miniature microscope that uses deep learning to image brain changes in aging and Alzheimer's disease.
This project tries to find out how immune problems and poor wound healing drive the disease disabling pansclerotic morphea.
This project tries to find out how a protein called partitioning defective 1c affects synaptic plasticity and learning.
This project studies what tumor genetics and immune features decide whether pancreas cancer responds to pembrolizumab and olaparib.
This project uses proteomics to study how prions cause synaptic dysfunction and neuronal degeneration in animal models and patient samples.
This project studies how the protein ezrin affects outflow resistance and intraocular pressure in glaucoma.
